entry.title: ohmyjev re-read at 0.14.0 (commit fbc4ea4; published 3 Nov 2026): its four other failure cells are unchanged (fail-open on error, timeout, malformed answer and missing key; acts anyway below its thresholds), and lockdown is still off by default. Its bypass cell keeps its term with new content: an opt-in shadow setting, off by default, runs the lockdown checks but only logs what they would block, and in-repo mkdir, touch, cp and mv now skip Jev. The failure map still counts 80 implementations; the checklist, Claude Code guardrails, coding agents and products pages carry the new pin.

Coding agents: @caph42/pi-jev-router 2.0.0 (pi) read in source at 75ad5b7 with pi 1.5.0 (f9a2636): Jev picks the complex or standard model for each request, pi applies the choice in code, and on any Jev failure it falls back to the standard model or keeps the current one. Counted on the page, under "Read in source; not on the failure map yet": 29 read in source, 15 counted, 10 not counted, 4 not settled. The failure map's 80 is unchanged. A dated list of 19 coding-agent projects seen 24 Oct to 8 Nov 2026 added as leads, not read in full.

Alternatives and the decision-API comparison: SubQ's docs and Terms now both say Decisions API inputs and outputs are deleted within 60 days (until at least 14 Oct 2026 they disagreed: 30 days in the Terms, kept until deleted in the docs). Cloudflare's Workers AI data-usage page, still dated 16 Oct 2026, also lists asynchronous or batch features and file or adapter uploads among its retention exceptions. OpenAI's Decisions API data controls re-read on 8 Nov 2026, unchanged. Card and copy block updated.

Frameworks: langchain-typesafe read at 0.0.2: failure path unchanged, with an optional classifier= argument on both experimental middlewares; pydantic-ai-slim 2.66.0's TypeSafe files are identical to 2.64.0. New releases noted, not re-read: @ai-sdk/typesafe-ai 3.0.35, ai 7.0.165, auto-mode 4.0.0; LiteLLM 1.108.3, whose notes do not mention TypeSafe or Jev.

Use cases: TypeSafe's docs index now lists 6 patterns, 26 cookbooks and 2 demos, adding "Verifying LLM answers against their source" (first listed between 7 Nov and 8 Nov 2026); its figures are TypeSafe's own. TypeSafe's models, Images, quickstart, legal and changelog pages were identical to the 7 Nov copies.

Access status rechecked 8 Nov 2026, 05:17 UTC: signups open, no free credit for new accounts, API operational, with no status event after 30 Oct; jev-latest and jev-preview still give jev-1.14.0 and jev-1.13.0 has no deprecation date; $0.042 per million input tokens. Uptime figure read as the 90-day window 99.883%. OpenCode's free ID and the six routes unchanged; OpenRouter's ZDR list has 1,117 endpoints, both Jev endpoints listed. Home keeps two notices.

New dated report: what changed for Jev builders, 7 to 8 November 2026 (ohmyjev 0.14.0, pi-jev-router, SubQ, Cloudflare and OpenAI data terms, TypeSafe's new cookbook, what was re-read unchanged and what was not checked).

TypeSafe's docs (first observed 7 Nov 2026; after the 2 Nov reads): the models page lists "Text, images" as the input of both jev-1.14.0 and jev-1.13.0, adds a Box question type that needs Jev 1.14 and drops its "Language support" section; a new docs changelog dates the Jev 1.14 entry 14 Oct 2026 and lists "Better multilingual support". The Images page still calls images not ready for production behind an opt-in header. Limitations, what is Jev, the decision-API comparison and other pages that described Jev's inputs or question types now say what the docs state; TypeSafe's cookbook figures updated as its own Reported figures. No image or Box request was sent.

Alternatives: Base Labs (Baseten's research lab) added as one hosted-API row: mammoth-1, elephant-1 and joey-1 on Baseten's Model APIs at $0.10, $0.035 and $0.01 per 1M input tokens as published, Baseten's zero-data-retention and no-training terms quoted, MIT weights published by Base Labs as a line inside the row, rank claims Reported and not matched. A different model; your data goes to Baseten. The benchmarks mention links to the row.

Versions and aliases: new title "Jev 1.14 vs 1.13 (TypeSafe AI): model IDs, jev-latest and aliases by route" (Google completes "jev 1.14 vs" to "jev 1.14 vs 1.13" on 7 Nov 2026), what differs between the two versions per TypeSafe's docs, and a dated list of eight GitHub issues and pull requests, read on 7 Nov, on staying on, pinning or leaving 1.13 (Reported). Aliases and route listings rechecked 7 Nov, unchanged.

Access status checked 7 Nov 2026, 15:29 UTC (previous check 2 Nov, 10:47 UTC; no check in between): signups open, no new-user credit, API operational; price, rate-limit wording and aliases unchanged; no status event listed for 31 Oct to 7 Nov; uptime figure read as the 90-day window 99.882%. The console sign-in page answered again (HTTP 200). TypeSafe's blog has a new post dated 3 Nov (about naming). Two notices shown.

OpenCode's jev-1.13-free re-read on 7 Nov 2026: still "Free" input and output, "available on OpenCode for a limited time", no end date or quota; data texts unchanged; its docs moved to opencode.ai/docs/console/models/. OpenRouter's ZDR endpoint list now has 1,119 endpoints, both TypeSafe endpoints listed.

Decision-API comparison and alternatives: the Jev input cell follows TypeSafe's models page ("Text, images"); cells due since 3 Nov re-read and unchanged carry the 7 Nov check date (d1-ultra, Mouse-1, Drex, Eevo terms, Microsoft-Decision-1 post and Learn page, OpenAI inputs and routes, SubQ Snap status and price); three cells that could not be settled keep their October dates. Laya v0.4.28 noted (contents not read).

Version notes: ohmyjev 0.14.0 (3 Nov) and langchain-typesafe 0.0.2 (5 Nov), released after the last read and not re-read; patch releases of @ai-sdk/typesafe-ai, ai, pydantic-ai-slim, deepeval, @openclaw/typesafe and n8n noted; LiteLLM's stable releases up to 1.108.2 do not include the eu/jev provider.

New dated report: what changed for Jev builders between 2 and 7 November 2026 (TypeSafe's docs on images and Box, Base Labs' decision models, who stayed on Jev 1.13, OpenCode's free ID, uptime, ZDR list and release lines), with what was re-read unchanged and what was not checked.

Failure map: ohmyjev read again at 0.13.2 (commit d307c39). Its Jev gates now run only with its lockdown setting on, which is off by default; the row describes lockdown mode, where a Jev error, a malformed answer or a missing key still lets the call through and calls below its cut-offs go ahead (terms unchanged). The bypass cell changed in content (default skip of every gate; auto-approve path removed; GitHub-write reminder by code). No count changed: 80 implementations. The checklist, copy block, self-check example and the Claude Code, coding-agent and products pages follow.

New dated block on where to use: OpenCode's docs list jev-1.13-free ("Free" input and output per 1M tokens, "available on OpenCode for a limited time") and jev-1.13 ($0.042 input) on OpenCode's own endpoint. Third-party route; not run by TypeSafe and not one of the six compared routes. OpenCode does not say which Jev version either ID serves; reported errors listed with their dates. Not tested.

Data privacy: OpenCode's two texts quoted side by side for jev-1.13-free (docs: providers follow a zero-retention policy and do not train, Jev not among the exceptions; Terms of 15 Aug 2026: Content from an unpaid account may be used to improve its services, and it does not control third-party providers' retention), with the note that OpenCode does not say which text controls. OpenRouter's ZDR endpoint list now names typesafe/jev-1.13-20260917 and typesafe/jev-1.14-20261014 (1,094 endpoints at 10:59 UTC on 2 Nov; 941 on 10 Oct).

Access status checked 2 Nov 2026, 10:47 UTC (previous check 31 Oct, 05:11 UTC; no check in between): signups open, no new-user credit, API operational; price, rate-limit wording and aliases unchanged; no status event listed for 31 Oct to 2 Nov; uptime figure read as the 90-day window 99.880%. The console sign-in pages returned an HTTP 403 block page and could not be read. New "Is Jev free?" box keeps TypeSafe's credit condition and OpenCode's third-party free ID apart. Two notices shown.

Decision-API comparison: Microsoft-Decision-1's catalog cells (text-only sentence, 32,768-token context, licence text) re-read on 2 Nov 2026 and unchanged; the cells re-read unchanged carry the 2 Nov check date. Laya v0.4.21 noted on alternatives and Laya vs Kev (contents not read).
